# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## From cand_0001 (SpreadsheetBench, empty-seed prose capability)

1. **An empty seed file is ambiguous in a way that changes the baseline's meaning.** `prompt.md` at
   0 bytes made the adapter send *no system message*, while a *missing* file would have fallen back
   to `_DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`. I only learned which by reading the adapter. Since the proposer is
   told not to edit the adapter, the framework should state in INSTRUCTIONS.md what the seed
   actually resolves to at runtime — or seed the current effective text so the diff is honest.

2. **The brief says "run no evaluation yourself", but the SAFE test requires evidence.** The only
   way I could check the riskiest edit (a code snippet inside the prompt) was to extract it and run
   it against gold workbooks read-only. That is clearly in the spirit of the rules but sits close to
   a line the brief draws hard. Worth saying explicitly: **read-only inspection of inputs/gold to
   verify an edit is expected and encouraged; what is forbidden is mutating the environment or
   scoring yourself.** Without that, a cautious proposer ships unverified prose.

3. **Breadth guidance and attribution guidance conflict, and the framework should pick.** I was
   told to make as many real fixes as possible ("a timid two-edit iteration is under-used"), and
   also that a rejection reports `broke={...}` per task. With 8 edits in one candidate, a rejection
   cannot be attributed to an edit. Either the gate should re-score with single edits ablated when
   it rejects a multi-edit candidate, or the brief should tell the proposer which side to err on.
   A cheap middle ground: ask the proposer to *rank its own edits by blast radius* in PROCESS.md
   (I did) and have the framework bisect from that ranking automatically.

4. **`LEDGER.md`, `RUNMAP.md`, `prior_iterations/`, `rejected.jsonl` and `history.jsonl` are all
   empty on iteration 1, but the brief reads as though they contain something.** Five files to open
   to learn "this is the first iteration". A one-line `RUNMAP.md` stub (`iteration 1 of N — no
   priors`) would save the round trip on every cold start.

5. **The trajectories are the only evidence, and their most decision-relevant fields are buried.**
   What decided this candidate was two aggregate counts (formula-writers 0/13; 39-of-40 never
   re-read their output), which I had to compute by parsing 40 JSON files. A generated
   `trajectories/SUMMARY.md` — per task: passed?, `test_case_results` vs
   `test_case_results_no_recalc`, turns used, distinct-code-blocks-submitted, whether the output was
   ever re-opened — would put the highest-leverage clusters in front of every proposer for free.
   The `results=[1]` / `no_recalc=[0]` disagreement in particular is a *ready-made* cluster label.

## From cand_0003 (SpreadsheetBench; 2 priors: one accept, one reject)

6. **cand_0001's item 3 above was not a hypothetical — it has now cost the run a measured win, and
   the framework can fix it cheaply.** cand_0002 shipped 6 edits, was rejected on
   `broke={2768, 51-12}`, and the framework **reverted all six — including the two that
   demonstrably fixed 227-40 and 267-18.** The run threw away two confirmed fixes to discard two bad
   clauses. Since the gate already re-scores candidates and already computes per-task deltas, the
   obvious addition is: **on rejection of a multi-edit candidate, ablate and re-score.** Even a
   single automatic pass that drops the edits the proposer ranked as UNBOUNDED/highest-blast-radius in
   PROCESS.md would have salvaged cand_0002's two fixes. Absent that, every rejected iteration is a
   total loss rather than a partial one, which makes the search far more expensive than it needs to
   be — and rationally pushes proposers toward timid one-edit candidates, in direct conflict with the
   brief's breadth mandate.

7. **`rejected.jsonl`'s reason string records the gate arithmetic but not the diagnosis, so the
   partial-credit signal has to be re-derived from traces.** The line for cand_0002 is
   `paired Δ̄=+0.0000 <= 0.2·SE=0.0101 …`. It does not say *which edit* or even carry the
   `broke`/`fixed` sets that LEDGER.md has. Including the per-task deltas (or a pointer to them) in
   the same record would let a successor triage from one file instead of cross-referencing three.

8. **The headroom can fall below the gate's own resolution, and the brief should say what to do
   then.** After cand_0001, 4 tasks remained failing (~0.10 of val) while the gate's stated
   resolvable effect size is `2·SE = 0.1013`. So even a *perfect* iteration fixing all four sits at
   the edge of detectability, and any candidate that fixes 2 while breaking 2 is guaranteed Δ≈0
   regardless of merit. The brief should either (a) surface this explicitly ("remaining headroom is
   N tasks vs a resolvable effect of M — expect noise-limited results"), or (b) increase trials on
   the few remaining failures when headroom shrinks, so a genuine 2-task fix can actually clear the
   bar. Right now a proposer can do everything right and still be indistinguishable from noise.

9. **Verification affordances differ between iterations of the same run, silently.** cand_0002
   verified its edits by executing them against the benchmark `init`/`golden` workbooks; from
   cand_0003's sandbox those paths hold only the single task id being run and no `*_golden.xlsx`
   exists anywhere. Nothing announced the change, so I spent time searching for something a prior
   iteration's JOURNAL said was available. Either mount the read-only gold set consistently for every
   proposer (it is the single strongest SAFE-test tool available) or state plainly in INSTRUCTIONS.md
   that it is unavailable, so the proposer goes straight to trace-based methods.

10. **`PROCESS.md` is snapshotted per candidate but seeded with the *previous* candidate's content.**
    I opened it expecting a template and found cand_0001's completed write-up, which I had to
    overwrite wholesale. Seeding it with the empty section headers (or with the prior version clearly
    fenced as `<!-- prior iteration, replace -->`) would remove the risk that a proposer edits
    around stale text and ships a PROCESS.md describing a different candidate's edits.

11. **State the acceptance bar in INSTRUCTIONS.md — proposers currently reverse-engineer it, and get
    it wrong.** The brief says only "clears a significance bar (a noise margin)". The real bar is
    `Δ̄ > k_se·SE` with **k_se = 0.2**, recoverable only by finding a *prior rejection's* verdict
    string in `rejected.jsonl` and reading `gate.py`. cand_0003's JOURNAL shows the cost of guessing:
    it quoted the *descriptive* `resolvable effect size 2·SE = 0.1013` as though it were the bar,
    concluded its 4-task headroom (0.10) was smaller than what the gate could resolve, and reshaped
    its whole iteration around a constraint that did not exist (the bar was ≈0.0101, 10× smaller).
    Printing `k_se`, the gate mode, `n_trials`, and the current bar in the run budget line would cost
    one sentence and would directly improve strategy selection.

12. **The "ship AS MANY fixes as you can / breadth is the goal" framing misfires at high val.** At
    0.975 with one failing task, maximum upside is +0.025 and one regression is −0.025. Breadth then
    means inventing edits for clusters that do not exist — the exact speculative behavior the same
    document spends several paragraphs forbidding. The two instructions collide, and the proposer must
    notice the collision to resolve it. Suggest scaling the framing to the measured headroom: when
    `failing_tasks <= 2`, say so — "this split is nearly saturated; prefer one verified fix and
    exhaustive blast-radius checks over additional edits."

13. **Point proposers at the gold workbooks explicitly (follow-up to item 9).** They are present at
    `…/capevolve-ci/spreadsheetbench-data/spreadsheetbench_verified_400/spreadsheet/<id>/1_<id>_{init,golden}.xlsx`.
    cand_0003 looked at `/mnt/data/spreadsheet/<id>/` — the path the *agent* sees at runtime, which is
    not populated for the proposer — and recorded in JOURNAL + INSIGHTS that gold was unavailable,
    degrading its verification to synthetic twins and propagating that belief forward. One line naming
    the proposer-side data root would have made two iterations' SAFE tests exact instead of
    directional. This is the single highest-value line the brief could add for this benchmark.

14. **Surface the champion's own `broke={...}` as the primary lead, with a pointer to the
    still-on-disk passing trace.** The failing-task block described 2768 only as "1 ALWAYS-failing
    task", when in fact the LEDGER shows it was *broken by the current champion* and a passing trace
    sits in `../cand_0003/trajectories/`. Diffing those two traces localized the defect immediately.
    Labelling such tasks "regressed by champion — prior passing trace at <path>" would turn the run's
    most informative signal from something a proposer has to piece together into something handed to it.

<!-- cap-evolve:framework-improvements-append-below -->

15. **Tell the proposer that every candidate's full rollouts are on disk — including the REJECTED
    ones — and point at the path.** This was the highest-leverage thing I found this iteration, and
    I found it by accident. `RUNMAP.md` offers each prior iteration's `PROCESS.md` + `diff.patch`,
    and the brief mentions `./trajectories/` for the *current* candidate — so the natural reading is
    that a rejected candidate's behavior is gone and only its diff and its `broke={...}` set survive.
    In fact `run_suite/rollouts/val/*__<candidate>__t0.json` holds all 40 trajectories for every
    candidate ever scored. That converts post-reject attribution from guesswork into measurement:
    diff the first assistant message per task between champion and rejected candidate, count how
    many changed, and you learn which edit in a multi-edit batch actually moved behavior. For
    cand_0004 the count was 40/40 for one edit and 1/40 for another — a distinction no amount of
    re-reading the diff would have produced. Suggested addition to `RUNMAP.md`: a
    `rollouts/<split>/*__<id>__t0.json` column, with one line saying rejected candidates' traces are
    retained and are the correct way to attribute a batch's regressions.

16. **The gate scores a batch, but the brief asks for breadth — say out loud how those interact as
    headroom shrinks.** The instructions strongly and repeatedly push breadth ("a timid one- or
    two-edit iteration is an under-used iteration"). That is correct early: at val 0.450 with 22
    tasks failing, 7 edits bought +0.450. It inverts near saturation. At val 0.975 there is one
    failing task, so headroom is 0.025 while one regression also costs 0.025 — and because the gate
    scores the whole candidate, a single unbounded edge discards the good edits shipped alongside it
    (cand_0002: fixed 2, broke 2, Δ+0.000, rejected). A proposer following the breadth instruction
    literally at that point is being pushed toward negative expected value. Suggestion: make the
    breadth directive headroom-aware — e.g. when the failing-task count is ≤2, state that a single
    maximally-bounded edit with everything else held byte-identical is the expected shape, and that
    it will not be read as under-use. Two of this run's five iterations were spent learning this
    empirically.

17. **Distinguish, in the edit-space description, artifacts that are CONSULTED from artifacts that
    are EXECUTED BY EVERY TASK.** The brief presents `prompt.md` (~40% of words) and
    `task_template.md` (~60%) as two comparable surfaces and nudges toward the larger one ("an
    iteration that only touches the first is leaving most of the agent's instruction surface
    untouched"). But their blast radii differ categorically: `prompt.md`'s Rule N subsections are
    reference text consulted when a condition applies, so a gated addition there can be bounded to a
    single task; `task_template.md`'s numbered procedure is walked by all 40 tasks, so **any** edit
    to it perturbs all 40 trajectories, however additive the wording. Measured: cand_0004's
    procedure edit changed the first assistant message on 40/40 tasks. Both of this run's rejects
    edited the numbered steps; neither accept restructured them. The word-count framing invites
    exactly the wrong inference. Suggestion: annotate the two files with their blast-radius class
    rather than their share of the word count.
